claims.text: A controlled post-sintering heat treatment can form uniformly dispersed, sub-50 nm coherent B2 nanoprecipitates in a tungsten-based refractory HEA.
The coherent nanoprecipitates will enhance electron-mediated heat transfer.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can preserve or improve the mechanical integrity of a tungsten-based refractory HEA.
The initial sintered tungsten-based HEA has a homogeneous single-phase matrix and properties suitable for use as a reactor intermediate layer.
Heating at approximately 900°C for 15–30 minutes in an inert atmosphere will promote nucleation and growth of coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
The proposed benefits will persist at operating temperatures of 800–1000°C under cyclic mechanical loading representative of plasma-facing component stresses.
The heat treatment will produce uniformly distributed, sub-50 nm coherent B2 nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates will bond coherently with the surrounding HEA matrix.
The nanoprecipitates will act as conduits for electron flow.
The nanoprecipitates provide high-electron-mobility pathways that increase thermal conductivity through electronic conduction.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces minimize electron scattering.
The coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion.
Coherent precipitate structures can reduce stress concentration and crack initiation while retaining strength and ductility.
The treated intermediate layer will have approximately 20% greater effective thermal conductivity than the untreated material.
The treated alloy will retain or improve yield strength and ductility under cyclic loading at 800–1000°C.
Current tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers have low thermal conductivity and develop comparatively large thermal gradients at plasma-facing operating temperatures.
Current tungsten-based HEA intermediate layers risk mechanical degradation under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads.
Outside 800–1000°C, over-precipitation or precipitate coarsening may negate the proposed benefits.
The optimal nanoprecipitate size distribution for increasing heat transfer without substantial electron scattering is uncertain.

contradictions.description: The mechanism confidently states that coherent nanoprecipitates minimize electron scattering, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that nanoprecipitate size may introduce significant electron scattering.
